title: Branching Beyond Leonardo: Height-Balanced Key-Ordered Trees in Swift
topic: Branching Beyond Leonardo: The Evolution of Tree Architecture Theory
author: Mateus Yonathan
journal: Polyglot Systems Lab Agentic Research Preprints

abstract: We present a Swift implementation of a height-balanced, key-ordered tree that generalizes classical B-tree concepts to a purely functional node layout. The design preserves the invariant that every internal node has between $b$ and $2b$ children, guaranteeing $O(\log_b N)$ search, insertion, and deletion. We formally prove the height bound and key-ordering invariant, and we analyze the static abstract syntax tree (AST) to confirm that the implementation satisfies the claimed $O(N)$ auxiliary memory and $O(\log N)$ amortized rebalancing cost. The source code is publicly available at \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/swift-systems-lab/tree/main/algorithms/20261109_050217_branching_beyond_leonardo__the}.
